title: Newton's Method for Systems
description: Multidimensional Newton's method, Jacobian, damped Newton, Gauss–Newton for nonlinear least squares.
html:
🧭 Newton's Method for Systems

1. The Newton Step

$$F(x) = 0,\; F: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R^n; \qquad DF(x_k)\,\Delta_k = -F(x_k), \quad x_{k+1} = x_k + \Delta_k$$

$DF$ = Jacobian, row $i$ = $\nabla F_i^T$. Solve a linear system (4.3), do not invert. For linear $F$: exact in one step.

Example $x^2 + y^2 = 4$, $xy = 1$

$DF = \begin{pmatrix}2x&2y\\y&x\end{pmatrix}$. Start $(2, 0.5)$: $(1.933333, 0.516667) \to (1.931853, 0.517637) \to (1.9318517, 0.5176381)$. Errors $6.8\cdot10^{-2}, 1.5\cdot10^{-3}, 1.1\cdot10^{-6}, 8\cdot10^{-13}$: quadratic.

2. Convergence and Dangers

  • Locally quadratic if $DF(x^*)$ is nonsingular and $DF$ is Lipschitz continuous.
  • $\det DF = 0$ (example: $y = \pm x$) ⇒ step not executable or huge; avoid symmetric starting values.
  • Damped Newton: $x_{k+1} = x_k + \lambda\Delta_k$, halve $\lambda$ until $\|F\|$ decreases.

3. Variants

  • Simplified Newton: freeze $DF(x_0)$, one LU decomposition, only linearly convergent.
  • Broyden: $B_{k+1} = B_k + \frac{(y_k - B_ks_k)s_k^T}{s_k^Ts_k}$, secant condition $B_{k+1}s_k = y_k$, superlinear.
  • Gauss–Newton: $J^TJ\Delta = J^Tr$ for $\min\|r(p)\|^2$; example $y = ae^{bt}$: sum of squares $5.254 \to 0.037$. Levenberg–Marquardt: $(J^TJ + \mu I)\Delta = J^Tr$.
  • Newton for $\nabla f = 0$ = Newton's method of optimisation with the Hessian.

4. Typical Mistakes

  • Setting up the Jacobian transposed.
  • Forgetting the sign at $-F$.
  • Forming $DF^{-1}$ explicitly instead of solving a system.
